subject: Renewal: 2027 commitment + conditional credits and pilot upsell
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@cloudware.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — initial framework

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the time today. As promised, I've attached a first-pass renewal framework that balances Cloudware's desire for predictable unit economics with the burst protection you asked about. High level: a 12-month committed plan, an optional 6-month pilot for the search-augmentation feature (upsell), and a conditional credit structure that activates when monthly consumption exceeds the committed baseline.

Key bullets from the attachment (Cloudware_Renewal_Offer_v4.pdf):
- Base commit: 1.2M tokens/month (12-month term).
- Base discount: 15% off list for committed usage.
- Burst credits: 10% credit on overage for first 20% above commit, 5% for next 30%.
- Price hold: maintain current per-token list for term if commit bumped by >=25% at signing.
- Pilot upsell: 3-month pilot for the search feature at a reduced embedding rate; if Cloudware converts, the pilot consumption counts toward the commit.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) We tighten the mutual action plan (attached MAT) around PO timing and onboarding credits.
2) Procurement (Alex) to confirm required PO window/format.
3) I can route a revised amendment once we have your PO and pilot decision.

I'll loop in Marissa (CS lead) so we can coordinate onboarding timing if you elect the pilot.

Thanks —
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0122

Attachments: Cloudware_Renewal_Offer_v4.pdf (proposal), MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (stub)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear structure. A couple of clarifications from our side before we move this to procurement:

- Can you break the economics into monthly invoice examples at 80%, 100%, 130% of commit? Procurement needs a clear view on monthly spend variance.
- For the pilot: who owns the SOW for the analytics work? We prefer Redwood to cover the first 2 weeks of integration as a credit.
- Price hold: procurement wants the hold to be explicit in the amendment (not just in the proposal).

Alex — procurement requirements: PO lead time is 45 days from signature and the PO number must appear on the DocuSign amendment.

If you can confirm the monthly examples and confirm the onboarding credit for the pilot, we can move to PO prep.

Samira / Alex —

Thanks — attached is a quick one-pager in the MAT that shows monthly invoice examples at 80%, 100%, and 130% of the commit (pulled into the MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx). Summary here for convenience: 

- 80% usage (960k tokens): Invoice = (commit discount applied) => baseline charge = $X, net after 15% discount = $Y; no burst credits.
- 100% usage (1.2M tokens): baseline charge = $X_full, net after 15% = $Y_full.
- 130% usage (1.56M tokens): baseline = $X_full + overage(360k tokens) ; overage credit = 10% credit applied to first 240k tokens, then 5% on next 120k.

I'll have Finance produce a line-item example with dollar amounts if you prefer; the percentages above should map directly to your existing forecast tooling.

Pilot onboarding credit: Redwood can cover the first 80 engineering hours of integration as a one-time credit (to address Samira's ask for two weeks). We'll show that as an onboarding credit on the first invoice.

Amendment language for price hold (proposed clause):
"If Customer increases the committed monthly token volume by at least twenty-five percent (25%) at the time of signing, Redwood shall maintain the per-token list price for the duration of the 12-month term notwithstanding otherwise scheduled price adjustments."

If that reads ok, I'll have legal prepare an amendment for signature and Marissa will confirm CS/Ops onboarding timing. I can also include the PO timing language Alex requested (45-day lead).

Ben
